risks.note: Named by management as a key focus area of the Enterprise Risk Management framework. Crompton's core categories are directly exposed to BEE star-rating and efficiency labelling changes, and product roadmaps (BEE star-rated fans and water heaters) must be re-engineered whenever norms tighten.

Explicitly listed among the key risk focus areas. Quality failures would hit brand trust and warranty cost, which is why the Company embeds quality via the SAP Quality Module, stage-gate NPD validation, reliability testing, plant and supplier Kaizens and QC Story defect-reduction projects.

Flagged as a key ERM focus area. Exposure spans decarbonisation, resource efficiency, responsible product design, zero waste to landfill and monitoring of air, water and noise parameters across facilities and the supply chain, with regulatory and reputational consequences if standards slip.

Listed as a key risk focus area. Growth depends on proprietary platforms NUCLEUS (premium efficiency and BLDC-led participation) and XTECH (reliability and durability); failure to keep translating consumer insight into differentiated products would erode premiumisation and category leadership.

Named among key risk focus areas. As purchase decisions shift toward experience, after-sales support and brand credibility, weak service delivery across the retailer and service network directly threatens brand salience and repeat demand.

Management states it tracks and mitigates risks across product, brand and operational areas. Brand Crompton is the central asset behind premiumisation and go-to-market excellence, so dilution of brand salience is treated as a tracked enterprise risk.

Management identifies inventory discipline as a risk to be managed, addressed through Project ForeSight digital forecast enrichment to align production schedules with demand, standardised SOPs, rigorous vendor onboarding, Butterfly warehouse integration and QR-code Track-and-Trace across all product lines and 30 warehouses.

Demand is culturally anchored in weddings, festivals, births and the harvest season, and gold doubles as a savings asset, particularly in rural India.
